data.name: CBS Keeps J.J. Watt in Top NFL Booth for Weeks 2 and 3, No Romo Return
data.summary: CBS Sports announced its NFL broadcast teams for Weeks 2 and 3, with Watt, Nantz, and Tracy Wolfson handling the Patriots-Steelers game on Sept. 20 and Ravens-Cowboys from Rio on Sept. 27. Romo remains absent following his July arrest on an operating while intoxicated charge, to which he pleaded no contest earlier this month, and CBS has shared no return timeline. Other crews feature voices like Kevin Harlan on Chiefs-Dolphins and Ian Eagle on Bengals-Steelers, as the network relies on Watt's solid early performances. Fans showed excitement for matchups like the top team in Pittsburgh, blending anticipation with speculation on Romo's future.

Tight end Dallas Goedert grabbed two touchdowns, rookie Dontayvion Wicks scored in his debut, and the defense stopped a late two-point try. Orlovsky described the effort as 'solid' with room to grow in coordinator Sean Mannion's Shanahan-inspired scheme, drawing pushback from fans who see higher potential after last year's Super Bowl run and insist the team will rack up wins.

data.hook: With the clock ticking down, Darnell Washington caught the ball and planted Falcons safety Xavier Watts into the turf with a stiff arm that looked straight out of basketball.
data.name: Darnell Washington's Vicious Stiff Arm Steals Steelers' Win Over Falcons
data.summary: In the Steelers' 20-13 victory over the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday, tight end Darnell Washington sealed the win late in the fourth quarter with a 15-yard catch and a brutal stiff arm on third-and-three. The 6-foot-7 powerhouse, often called 'Mount Washington,' sent Watts flying, prompting teammate Pat Freiermuth to say from across the field, 'This is not gonna be good for that kid. He dirted him into the ground.' Fans lit up timelines calling it the stiff arm of the week, with jokes about dribbling a defender like a basketball, turning the play into the game's defining highlight despite Washington's modest two catches for 18 yards.

data.hook: Zay Flowers dazzled with 150 yards and a touchdown before a hamstring tweak sent him to the sideline early. The Ravens still cruised to victory, showcasing their new defensive edge.
data.name: Ravens Dominate Colts 41-23 in Minter's Debut Behind Pass Rush and Flowers' Big First Half
data.summary: Baltimore opened the Jesse Minter era with a 41-23 rout of Indianapolis, fueled by 506 total yards, an explosive first-half offense, and a pass rush that pressured Daniel Jones on 52.9% of dropbacks. Trey Hendrickson shone in his Ravens debut with eight or nine pressures, while Flowers exited day-to-day after his career-best half—Coach Minter expressed optimism ahead of an MRI. Colts added Sauce Gardner, who locked down receivers in heavy man coverage, but fell short amid tackling woes and explosive plays allowed. Despite injuries to Flowers and Ja’Kobi Lane, Baltimore heads to face the Saints feeling strong on defense.

data.hook: Late in a tight game against the Bills, Henry To’oTo’o tackled tight end Dawson Knox and went down hard, needing help off the field with his shoulder.
data.name: Texans LB Henry To’oTo’o Out with Shoulder Injury After Bills Loss
data.summary: Houston Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans announced Monday that linebacker Henry To’oTo’o suffered a shoulder injury in the 36-31 season-opening loss to Buffalo and will miss some time. The 25-year-old starter, who had two tackles before exiting, was seen in a sling postgame; the team hasn't decided on injured reserve yet. This adds to Houston's injury woes with absences like Tank Dell and Braden Smith, as backup Jake Hansen stepped in during the game. The Texans face the Bengals at home in Week 2, testing their linebacker depth.
